# Wr003 — Final `END-ISO-10303-21;` without trailing newline

<!-- Auto-generated; edit `STEP_PROBLEM_CATALOG.md` instead. -->

**Section**: §12.13 (`12-13-writer-pathology`)  
**Fixture**: [`step-examples/12-13-writer-pathology/Wr003.stp`](../../step-examples/12-13-writer-pathology/Wr003.stp)  
**Sender**: Older Siemens NX export and several in-house writers  

## Sources
- prostep ivip CAx-IF
- OCCT forum "concatenating two STEP files produces unparseable result"

## Description

The closing `END-ISO-10303-21;` token is emitted without a trailing newline. The spec does not require one (it requires only the closing marker), so the file is well-formed. But concatenation of two such files produces `END-ISO-10303-21;ISO-10303-21;` on a single line, which trips a class of crude scripts that grep for `^ISO-10303-21;`. Bug-reporter language: "can't concat two STEPs", "POSIX text-file rule violated", "no newline at end of file".

## Reproducer recipe

Part-21 file ending with the bytes `END-ISO-10303-21;` and no `0x0A` after.

## Expected kernel behavior

parsers must accept (the spec permits this); downstream tooling that concatenates files should add its own separator.

## Notes

A POSIX-text-file convention (text files end with newline) but not a Part-21 requirement.
